title: MA8-15211
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: The claimant, XXXXX XXXXXX XXXXX, is a citizen of Mexico. He arrived in Canada on XXXXXX, 2010, and claimed refugee protection the same day, under sections 96 and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).
The claimant alleged that, in XXXX 2008, after he and his wife had separated, he received threats from her lover.

The claimant alleged that he continued receiving death threats from his wife's lover in XXXX 2008, telling him to move elsewhere. Also during that same month, someone tried to run him over with a car.
The claimant alleged that he received threats from this same individual in XXXXXX 2008 and that, fearing for his life, he left Mexico and came to Canada.

Having examined all the testimonial and documentary evidence, the panel determines that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of the Act, for the reasons that follow.
The panel has a copy of the claimant's passport and is satisfied as to his identity.
The panel finds that the claimant's credibility is seriously undermined by his testimony, for the following reasons.

The claimant testified that he fears his ex-wife's lover, who allegedly started threatening him after he and his wife separated in XXXX 2008. He added that his aggressor was a hit man for a drug trafficker associated with the "Los Zetas" group. He claimed to know this because of the things his aggressor told him he had done.

He was asked to explain why, in his statement in his Personal Information Form (PIF) (question 31), dated October 22, 2008, no mention is made of his aggressor being a member of Los Zetas. The claimant responded that no one had ever translated his statement from French into Spanish for him and that he had only been asked to sign his statement where indicated. He added that this took place 20 days after his arrival and that he did not know what to say.

The panel does not accept the claimant's explanations for this omission, which is essential to understanding his refugee protection claim. When he made his statement on October 22, 2008, the claimant was already being represented by a lawyer, and no officer of the Government of Canada was present or asked him questions about his reasons for leaving his country.

In addition, the claimant signed that the information provided in his statement was complete, true and correct and that everything had been interpreted to him. The claimant, who filed numerous documents in June 2011 in support of his refugee protection claim, also did not take the opportunity to correct or explain at the start of the hearing certain points in his statement, even though he stated today that he signed a document without knowing what was in it. That seriously undermines the credibility of the claimant's allegations.

When he arrived in Canada, the claimant was met by a border services officer in Toronto on XXXXX, 2008. During that meeting, the claimant stated that he had come to visit a friend in Montréal. When asked by the panel why he did not claim refugee protection in Canada right then, the claimant testified that he never stated that he had come to Canada as a visitor and that he had come to claim refugee protection.

Asked to explain why he did not claim refugee protection until the end of the interview on XXXXX, 2008, after the officer had told him that he would have to return to his country, the claimant still responded that he had never stated that he had come as a visitor and that there had been a great deal of pressure during that meeting. He also stated that he did not know why the officer would have written something like that.

After filing his refugee protection claim on XXXXX, 2008, the claimant met another Citizenship and Immigration Canada officer the next day. He stated again that he had come as a visitor and that he planned to claim refugee protection in Montréal.

The panel does not accept the claimant's explanations regarding his failure to take the opportunity to claim refugee protection when it was presented to him upon his arrival in Toronto. The claimant testified that he knew about the possibility of claiming refugee protection in September 2008 and that he did nothing when he arrived and only took the opportunity after an officer told him that he would have to return to his country. Also, the claimant's explanations that he never stated that he had come to Canada as a visitor contradicted the evidence on file (see the officer's notes attached to IMM 5500 F). In fact, the claimant, the day after he arrived in Toronto, met with another officer and confirmed having stated that he had initially come as a visitor.
Finally, during those meetings on XXXXX and XX, 2008, no reference was made to his aggressor's ties to the "Los Zetas" group.

The panel is of the opinion that, in this context, the claimant's behaviour was not consistent with that which any reasonable person would adopt if he or she was apparently receiving death threats from an individual who was a killer with ties to the "Los Zetas" group.
This seriously undermines the credibility of the claimant's allegations.
Because the claimant's testimony was not trustworthy on some key elements of his refugee protection claim, the panel did not believe his story about the threats against him.
In addition, nothing in the evidence, including the claimant's testimony, suggests that the claimant might be persecuted on one of the grounds set out in the Act.
For those reasons, and after examining the evidence as a whole, the panel determines that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection."

Therefore, his claim for refugee protection is rejected.
